en.heading: 20 October: Philippine-British Friendship Day changed its date
en.origin: Philippine-British Friendship Day highlights historical, cultural, political and economic links between the Philippines and the United Kingdom, including diplomacy and cooperation between communities. Proclamation No. 381 established the annual day on 7 December in 2000. This was the first modern recurring presidential recognition, not the date used by today's national calendar. Proclamation No. 1592, signed 20 August 2008, amended the earlier decree and moved the observance to 20 October from 2008 onward to coincide with the inauguration of a new British Embassy.

en.heading: 21 October: National Archives Day recalls the Bureau founded in 1901
en.origin: National Archives Day invites people to recognize the importance of public records, historical documents and careful preservation of government information for accountability and collective memory. The Philippine Commission established a Bureau of Archives under the Department of Public Instruction on 21 October 1901. This founding event later supplied the historical anniversary for archives work. Proclamation No. 660, signed 27 September 1995, officially made every 21 October National Archives Day. The original bureau's establishment in 1901 and the modern recurring proclamation in 1995 must not share one undifferentiated founding year.

en.heading: 11 November: the Underground River award and a later national observance
en.origin: Puerto Princesa Underground River Day celebrates the protected natural site in Palawan, known for its underground river system and biodiversity. It draws on public interest in conserving the landscape. On 11 November 2011 the site was chosen among the New Seven Wonders of Nature in a private international campaign. This selection event was not a Philippine presidential decree or the creation of the natural site. Proclamation No. 816 of 3 July 2014 made every 11 November Puerto Princesa Underground River Day. Separate annual local proclamations, such as a special non-working day for 11 November 2025 in Puerto Princesa City, do not turn the national observance into a permanent nationwide holiday.

en.heading: 25 October: the Military Academy chose its revolutionary-era founding
en.origin: The Philippine Military Academy traces its earliest roots to the Academia Militar founded in Malolos on 25 October 1898 under President Emilio Aguinaldo's revolutionary government, while the modern academy evolved through later institutions. During the American colonial period an officers' school of the Philippine Constabulary was established on 17 February 1905. That later institution once supplied the Academy's official foundation-day calendar. Proclamation No. 35 signed 13 October 1998 replaced the 17 February anniversary with 25 October, following historical research supported by the National Historical Institute. The 1998 decision corrected the commemorative date rather than founding a new academy.

Durante il periodo coloniale statunitense una scuola ufficiali della Constabulary fu fondata il 17 febbraio 1905. In precedenza tale evento determinava la data celebrativa dell'Accademia. en.heading: 12 August: the National Library's roots begin with a royal order in 1887
en.origin: The National Library of the Philippines preserves printed and recorded materials, books and documentary heritage that support public research, reading and the transmission of Filipino cultural memory. Royal Order No. 689 of 12 August 1887 established the Museo-Biblioteca de Filipinas in Manila, which the National Library identifies as its earliest institutional origin. This is the date used for the current founding anniversary. A separate American Circulating Library opened publicly on 9 March 1900; Public Act No. 96 of 5 March 1901 then reorganized and transferred library functions. Later names included Philippine Library and National Library, so the 1887 date and the 1900 public-library movement remain distinct.
